Sensing, computing, and feedback in a wallet-sized patch.

Sensing, computing, and feedback stack into something the thickness of a few credit cards. It wakes on skin contact, reads every compression as you give it, and answers with light. Nothing leaves the device.

Tap the patch. See what the rescuer sees.

Press the space bar or click the patch at the pace you would actually compress. CPRight reads your rate the same way the onboard processor does, by timing the interval between compressions.

One side is the device. The other side is the instructions.

A bystander gets no briefing and no second try. Everything they need is printed on the face they are already looking at.

It fits where help already lives.

It started with a question.

A simple solution to a big problem.

  1. 01

    It began on a couch

    Deeya Sharma and Nikhita Vaddineni were talking about a finding neither could shake. Women are significantly less likely to receive bystander CPR than men. Hesitation about physical contact, uncertainty about anatomy, fear of liability. The obvious first answer was to fix the training.

  2. 02

    ReviveHer

    So Sharma and Vaddineni founded ReviveHer, a breast attachment for CPR manikins, to confront a blind spot the medical community had largely ignored and to show how design and training could change the way people respond.

  3. ReviveHer, the project that led here.
  4. 03

    A bigger problem underneath

    Going down that route surfaced something larger. It was not only who received CPR. Most people receiving CPR were having bad outcomes, because the CPR being delivered simply was not effective. Even trained responders lose rate, depth, and rhythm under real pressure.

  5. 04

    Four people, three months, one prototype

    Joined by Shubham Bansal and Prisha Hemani committed to the same problem, the team set out to build something simple enough for any bystander, cheap enough to be everywhere and practical enough to raise CPR quality in a real emergency. A working prototype came together in three months.

  7. 05

    What we are building toward

    Hunter McKay and Nate Snyder joined the team to put CPRight inside every AED cabinet, first aid kit and EMS bag, and in the pocket of everyone who has ever taken a CPR class. Lifesaving technology should be simple, affordable and there when seconds matter.

For investors

Where CPRight starts, how adoption grows from there, and the clinical and industry stakeholders we are in conversation with.
See the investor page

Building a scalable path to better CPR performance.

CPRight begins in CPR training, where feedback is the entire point of the room. Everything else we are building, the clinical work, the institutional relationships and the partnerships, is what turns that starting point into broader adoption.

Where we start

We are initially focused on CPR training environments, where consistent feedback and practical skill-building can help address gaps in compression quality. It is also where a device earns its evidence without making a clinical claim about a patient, which is why almost every conversation we have had points back to it.

The adoption pathway

Where a device like this can go, informed by the conversations further down this page. Read it as a direction we are working toward, not a schedule we are committing to.

  1. 01

    CPR training institutions

    Classrooms and certification programs, where every student needs to know whether their compressions were actually good enough.

  2. 02

    Clinical validation and FDA clearance

    Human and multi-center testing, working toward a Class II 510(k). CPRight is an investigational device today and we say so on every page.

  3. 03

    Higher-risk and care settings

    Gyms and skilled nursing facilities, where trained staff, an AED on the wall and an at-risk population already coincide.

Steps 04 and 05 run in parallel
  1. 04

    Emergency response and AED partnerships

    EMTs and first responders, alongside the AED channel that already reaches schools, offices and transit hubs.

  2. 05

    Small business and workplace wellness

    We are also talking with HR leaders, B2B decision-makers across tech and healthcare, healthcare providers, and people living with heart disease, about a path into workplace wellness and benefits programs beyond large hospital systems.

  3. 06

    Everywhere people already gather

    Airports, homeowners associations, retirement communities, athletic departments, hotels, and even college dorms are all places we see as a natural home for CPRight, wherever a bystander might be the first person to respond.

The AED channel is the opening we are exploring.

More than 200,000 AEDs are bought each year in the US alone, moving through distributors who already sell into schools, offices and transit hubs. We sized CPRight to ride along in a cabinet that is already bought, installed and inspected on a schedule.

The regulatory picture.

CPRight is an investigational device. It is not FDA cleared and it is not for clinical use. We are working toward a Class II 510(k) pathway, and human and multi-center testing comes before any of that. Nothing on this site is a clinical claim.

The questions we get asked most.

Does this work on all body types?

AHA guidelines specify the same compression depth and rate regardless of age, weight, or body type. CPRight is designed around those universal standards rather than patient characteristics, so the feedback is equally valid across all bodies.

Why is CPRight single use?

A single use design eliminates cross contamination entirely. No cleaning, no sterilization cycles, no reprocessing protocols. Each unit is sterile out of the package and disposed of after use.

How do you know where to compress?

The patch includes a clear PALM HERE marker that guides hand placement visually, which removes one of the most common sources of error without requiring any instruction.

Why is there no app?

Survival falls about 10 percent for every minute quality CPR is delayed. Anything that adds setup time is paid for in survival: unlocking a phone, pairing over Bluetooth, waiting for an app to load. CPRight activates on skin contact and gives feedback from the first compression.
SURVIVAL PROBABILITY VS. TIME TO HIGH-QUALITY CPR

Why LEDs instead of audio?

Visual feedback produces better compression accuracy than audio in peer reviewed studies, 78 percent correct versus 65 percent. LEDs also work where cardiac arrests actually happen: noisy streets, crowded rooms, active ambulances. And unlike a metronome, LEDs show depth and rate at the same time with no translation required.

Does it interfere with an AED or EKG?

No. CPRight is designed to sit alongside AED pads, EKG leads, and patient monitors without electrical or mechanical interference, and it works alongside 911 dispatcher instructions and standard CPR training.

Is it cleared by the FDA?

Not yet. CPRight is an investigational device, and a Class II 510(k) pathway is planned. Nothing on this site is a clinical claim.

Privacy and cookie policy

Last updated September 2026. Placeholder language for build, have counsel review before launch.

What this covers

This policy explains what CPRight collects when you visit this site, how cookies are used, and how to change your choices. It does not cover the device itself, which stores nothing and transmits nothing.

What the device collects

Nothing. CPRight processes compression data on board and discards it. There is no wireless radio, no pairing, no logging, and no patient data of any kind leaves the patch.

What the site collects

If you submit the contact form we receive your name, organization, email, and message so we can reply. We keep that correspondence only as long as the conversation is useful and never sell it.

Cookies we use

Essential cookies remember your consent choice and keep the site functioning. Analytics cookies count page views in aggregate so we can see which pages EMS agencies, distributors, and press actually read. Functional cookies remember interface preferences. Analytics and functional cookies are only set after you accept them.

Your choices

You can accept all, accept essential only, or set each category individually, at any time, from the cookie preferences link in the footer. Clearing your browser storage resets your choice and the banner returns.

Contact

Questions about this policy, or a request to delete correspondence, go to cpright.it@gmail.com.
